採用・広告の製品.quote: A new funding round or a new hire gives you a reason to reach out this month. Gelee watches for these and times the first message.
Hiring 3 SDRs
Viewed your pricing, 3x
“I had 3 reps prospecting by hand. Now I close 23 meetings a quarter without touching it.”
“I tried every LinkedIn tool going. With Gelee, prospects think I wrote the messages myself.”
Upload your leads and do-not-contact list, and pick up where you left off.

An agency that promises clients a fixed number of meetings. The platform will not set a goal above 20 booked calls a month for any workspace, however many seats it runs, and nobody here will promise a number above it either.

Every table in the platform is scoped to one organisation, and a client is one organisation. Seats, campaigns, prospects, replies, blacklist and bookings for Client A live under Client A and nowhere else. Your people are added as members of each workspace they work on, and a member of more than one sees a workspace switcher in the sidebar.

The practical effect is isolation by default. A seat that LinkedIn restricts stops sending and re-warms on its own; the other seats in that workspace and every other workspace carry on. A person on one client’s do-not-contact list is still contactable for a different client, unless you add them there too.

A newly connected seat sends at 25% of its budget for days 1 to 3, 50% through day 7, 75% through day 14 and full rate after that. The ramp covers invitations, messages, comments, InMails, profile views and searches together. A seat that LinkedIn flags is re-warmed rather than resumed, and after any cooldown it comes back at 25, 50 and 75% over six days.
Approval first, autonomy earned

Nothing launches without the client’s written approval of the targeting and the message sequence. Once live, every reply a prospect sends is drafted in the client’s voice and posted to that client’s Slack channel with three buttons: Approve & Send, Edit, Skip. An edit feeds back into the voice.
Onboarding a new client takes under a week

Expectations are set on that call and they are not guarantees. Accounts ramp for two to four weeks, results are not judged before 100 invitations, and an acceptance rate of 15 to 30% once settled is treated as healthy. Below 15% after 100 invitations, the list or the seat’s own profile is what gets fixed.

One channel for the conversation with you and the team, one for the SDR bot where every drafted reply lands with its Approve, Edit and Skip buttons. The client can sit in both or leave the second to you. A monthly report is generated for each workspace from the same event log the dashboard reads.

Sending on that seat stops and it is re-warmed from 25% rather than resumed at the rate that caused the problem. The client’s other seats keep running, and other clients are unaffected. The seat’s status and the reason are visible on the accounts page, and a disconnect posts once to that client’s channel.
Who approves the messaging, me or the client?

The client, in writing, before launch; a verbal yes on a call is not enough for the team to switch a campaign on. Day to day, replies are drafted and whoever sits in the SDR channel approves, edits or skips them. Which classes of message run without approval is decided by the approval record itself, as described above.
How many meetings should I promise a client?

Do not promise a count. The platform’s default monthly goal is 5 booked calls for one seat, 8 for two, 10 for three and 20 for four or more, and it refuses to store a goal above 20 for any workspace. What we publish is measured: see the benchmarks page for accept, positive reply and booking rates with the period and sample attached.

Yes. Every draft is a suggestion until someone approves it; your team can edit or skip any of them, or reply directly in the inbox. If that is all you want, though, a per-seat sender is cheaper, and we say so on the switching guides.
Written in the third person, like a press release, with your credentials and achievements up front. Best for fundraising, hiring and podcast intros.
To prevent abuse and to occasionally share new tools and product updates with you. We don't sell your data, and you can unsubscribe at any time.

You pay per LinkedIn account, per month: $149 for 1 or 2 accounts, $118 for 3 to 5, $100 for 6 to 12 and $89 for 13 to 25. Every account gets the full product. Done for you, and anything over 25 accounts, is priced on a call.

Every LinkedIn account includes 1,750 credits a month, in one pot your whole workspace shares. They cover turning a LinkedIn URL into full profile details, and the AI SDR, AI variables and Ask Gelee (the AI can use up to 500 of them). A mobile number costs 44 credits and a verified work email 2, only when we find one. Need more? Add credits in the app, from 2¢ each.
Is there a setup or onboarding fee?
Yes, add accounts at any time and the price per account drops as you cross each band. Removing accounts needs 30 days' notice.
